newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY TO CUT IMPORT SURCHARGE TO 4PCT FROM 6PCT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY TO CUT IMPORT SURCHARGE TO 4PCT FROM 6PCT.

text.p: Hungary on Thursday said it would cut the surcharge on all imported goods from six to four percent from March 10.
"The government decided to cut the import surcharge by a further two percent with effect from March 10," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told reporters.

The government first introduced an eight percent import surcharge in March 1995 as part of its austerity programme which succeeded in reining in the country's soaring current account and trade deficits.
Last year it announced it would honour its international obligations to phase out the tax completely by July 1 1997.
It introduced two one-percentage-point cuts in 1996 and said it planned three reductions of two points each in 1997, on January 1, April 1 and June 30.
However, the January cut was postponed.
